title: When a more cyclic majority tournament is more probable
description:
Unrefereed research candidate. When many voters each rank a fixed set of candidates independently and uniformly at random (the impartial-culture model, the standard yardstick of voting theory), the head-to-head majorities form a tournament: for each pair, an arrow from the majority winner to the loser. A cyclic triple is a rock-paper-scissors loop (A beats B, B beats C, C beats A), the pattern behind Condorcet's paradox.

Question. Harrison-Trainor (Mathematical Social Sciences, 2022; Conjecture 6.3 of the arXiv version) conjectured that, in the limit of many voters, a labelled tournament with fewer cyclic triples (equivalently, larger linearity, the sum of squared win counts) is always the more probable one. He checked it for up to five candidates.

Main results. (1) The conjecture is false. For every odd t there are tournaments on 14t candidates in which the tournament with 3t3 more cyclic triples is 23t2+o(t2) times as probable. Splitting candidates into ordered blocks explains why: the probability cost is governed by pairs of candidates whose latent strengths must be nearly equal (about a factor of two per pair), while cyclic triples are governed by triples, and the two counts can order block structures oppositely. (2) A rigorous rational certificate gives an explicit pair on 78 candidates: the tournament with three more cyclic triples is more than 105 times as probable, and the reversal persists for isomorphism classes (ratio above 3.3). (3) Monte Carlo computation, which is not a proof, finds no reversal on seven or fewer candidates and finds reversals on 13 candidates (by about 1%) and 14 candidates (by a factor of about 2.7). (4) The extremal half of the conjecture is true: the transitive tournaments are exactly the most probable ones, for every number of candidates and for a wide class of paired-comparison models. (5) Part II, for round robins: for any fixed latent-type comparison model with probabilities strictly between zero and one, either the win totals determine every outcome's probability (the Bradley–Terry case) or a typical outcome shares its win totals with outcomes exponentially more and less probable on the scale of the number of pairs; a conditional test built from directed triangles is exactly calibrated at every vector of win totals and detects every fixed departure of this kind from a single round robin. (6) With one observation per pair, the minimax Bradley–Terry–Luce test of Makur and Singh is impossible at constant separation; whether a constant number of observations per pair suffices remains open.

Credit. The conjecture is Harrison-Trainor's; the Gaussian limit is due to Harrison-Trainor and to Hązła, Mossel, Ross and Zheng; the qualitative characterisation of score-determined models to Lauritzen and to Iyer; the masking construction to Rastogi, Balakrishnan, Shah and Singh; the replication question to Makur and Singh.

Limits. Impartial culture is a mathematical null model, not a description of real electorates. All election results are in the many-voter limit; no finite electorate size is given. The smallest counterexample is not determined: certified at 78 candidates, and between 8 and 13 on the numerical evidence. The results of Part II hold for a fixed model, and the tests have modest power at league sizes.

Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF); an exact rational certificate (standard library); exhaustive enumerations for five and up to six candidates; checks of the scan and spectral tests; the seeded power study; the Monte Carlo small-case study; recorded outputs; the bibliography, a machine-readable index, a research-gate record, a review summary, a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. Every certificate check exits with an error on failure, also under python -O.

Assurance. Written proofs with an exact rational certificate and exhaustive small-case checks. Internal AI-assisted review only: five Claude reviewer roles in two calls, the lead's replay of the rational certificate and every check script with a negative control, one revision round with extensions, then a re-review and proof audit of the changed proofs. No Astra/Codex review took place. This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Text CC0-1.0; code MIT.
